a statistically random particle orientation is defined as the uniform distribution of the particle orientation over the entire 3D unit sphere and that the corresponding orientation-averaged scattering matrix has the property that its diagonal elements are equal and its off-diagonal elements are zero.

the orientation-averaging process is linear and commutative with respect to any linear combination of orientation-averaged scattering properties, and that it is invariant to any rotation of the coordinate system.

the orientation-averaging procedure for the scattering matrices of nonspherical particles is equivalent to the averaging over the three Euler angles and that the extinction matrix is orientation independent.
